newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chip firms drive Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip firms drive Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse closed its two-hour session on Monday with higher prices driven mainly by blue chips, including ONA Group, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 435.31, up 0.19 percent on the previous session.
ONA group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate which has stakes in 100 companies, was traded at 475 dirhams, up three dirhams compared with Friday's session.
Its subsidiary Lesieur, one of main edible oil firms, gained 26 dirhams to close at 1,200 dirhams.
"Generally speaking, the market pursues its upward trend...Active trading in blue chip companies was the engine behind Monday's rise," a trader said.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, rose 10 dirhams to close at 320 dirhams.
Ciments de Meknes cement firm, gained 20 dirhams in one session to close at 689 dirhams, a bourse official said.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, and Societe Nationale d'Investissement, a market largest capitalisation companies, were not traded.
The volume on the official market dropped to 27.2 million dirhams from 56.1 million on Friday's session.
